answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate and 14-day expiration window create urgent pressure, but the 94% volume utilization means we cannot afford delivery disruption. Memory_c4 demonstrates that renegotiation at renewal successfully recovered margin through benchmarking—this is our highest-probability, lowest-risk lever given the compressed timeline. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing without narrowing scope; combining aggressive renegotiation with extended terms could satisfy the cost mandate while locking in stability. Verifying c4's benchmarking approach will validate whether we have the data to push hard on both price and terms in the next 14 days. Switching vendors (c2) or deferring (c5) risk either onboarding delays or budget overruns we cannot absorb. Adding a second source (c3) does not address the primary cost mandate. Negotiation with incumbent, backed by market intelligence, is fastest to execution and preserves the integration stability we rely on at high utilization.
